column1: # OUTSIDE_SPITBOL_BASELINE.tsv -- snoflake_suite: shipped fixtures that are OUTSIDE the graded baseline
# because the ONE SNOBOL4 ORACLE does not answer them. Written coo 2026-09-08 on the ceo ruling of
# 17:39 CDT over Lon 2026-09-07 (one oracle, one feature set: SPITBOL, our x64 fork, sbl -bf) and the
# FACT RULE NO COMPATIBILITY SWITCH FOR ANY SCRIP LANGUAGE (RULES sec Oracles, CEO-391): what the
# oracle refuses, or only another implementation provides, is outside the baseline -- named here with
# its reason, OUT OF THE DENOMINATOR, never hidden and never xfail.
# Census: the progress table at SCRIP b2660262e corpus c030d241f (coo run 2026-09-08 17:32 CDT), the
# runner test_snoflake_suite.sh, per-program m3 rows. 180 shipped = 99 PASS + 38 FAIL + 1 CRASH + 42
# here. With these 42 out, the suite row reads 99/138 and the 39 FAIL+CRASH are the live bug population.
# ERRNO  : sbl -bf ITSELF ERRORS on the fixture and SCRIP raises the SAME ERROR NUMBER; only the listing
#          stream differs. The oracle does not produce a runnable answer to compare against, so the
#          fixture cannot be graded by stream equality. These 36 are exactly the rows of NARROW.tsv --
#          they were being counted inside graded_narrow, which lib_inventory.sh warns is a comparison
#          narrower than the claim the percent makes. They are recorded in BOTH files on purpose:
#          NARROW.tsv says how they were compared, this file says they are out of the denominator.
# NSTD   : @nonstandard fixture -- implementation-defined output, rc=0 against sbl -bf, so there is no
#          oracle answer to be right or wrong about.
